major_concerns: Single frozen LLM limits generality — results may not transfer across model families.
Simulator simplifications may overstate vulnerability vs real networks (external validity).
Adversary construction risks producing unrealistic/degenerate intents if not carefully constrained.
required_design_repairs: Add at least one secondary LLM family or lightweight model-ensemble check to assess transferability or clearly justify single-model choice.
Specify and publish complete adversary-generation procedures, seeds, and constraints; include human-review step to avoid degenerate/unrealistic adversaries.
Document simulator fidelity and include sensitivity tests (e.g., vary topology size/vendor commands) to bound external-validity claims.
Pre-register exact verifier rules and taxonomy mapping from verifier diagnostics to safety violations.

major_concerns: Error-seeding procedure may not reflect natural LLM error distributions (construct validity).
Feedback formats may inadvertently train to verifier idiosyncrasies rather than generalize.
Evaluation budget (max iterations) must be justified for power and practical operator workflows.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register and justify error-seeding distribution; include example tasks drawn from public datasets or prior benchmarks.
Define precise feedback-format schemas (message templates, fields) and publish examples so others can reproduce.
Include subgroup analyses and power/sample-size calculations; justify max-iteration budget and stopping rules.
Add a small generalization holdout: tasks not seen during prompt/template tuning to test overfitting to verifier hints.

major_concerns: Privacy/retention implications of provenance-rich logs are noted but insufficiently operationalized (legal/PII concerns).
Simulated incidents may simplify reconstruction; production rollback complexity (stateful systems, external dependencies) underrepresented.
Storage/compute cost normalization lacks real-world calibration; results may be sensitive to normalization constants.
required_design_repairs: Explicitly define provenance schema fields and justify minimal vs rich sets; include privacy-preserving synthetic-data design and redaction policies.
Provide sensitivity analyses for storage/compute normalization constants and include raw resource metrics (bytes, CPU-seconds) in addition to normalized cost.
Augment incident simulations with higher-fidelity state (multiple dependent devices, timed cascading effects) or clearly delimit external-validity limitations.
Pre-register reconstruction algorithm pseudocode and failure definitions; publish artifacts and hashes to enable reproducibility.

major_concerns: Cost normalization and verifier-strength definitions are subjective and will drive conclusions if not transparently parameterized.
Simulated arrival processes and contention effects may not reflect operational burstiness or multi-tenant effects.
Interaction effects (arrival_rate × verifier_strength) may require larger runs for stable estimation than planned.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register and justify normalization constants; report raw CPU-seconds and model-call counts alongside normalized costs and run sensitivity sweeps.
Define verifier-strength concretely (exact checks run, time/CPU profiles) and publish verifier implementations/configurations.
Increase planned run counts or include bootstrap/CIs to ensure stability of Pareto front estimation; precompute power/sample targets for key comparisons.
Include at least one realistic burstiness arrival pattern and a sensitivity analysis for different workload shapes.
